misconceptions.description: Assuming AI automatically fixes weak instructional design
misconceptions.trigger: learner treats advanced technology as a substitute for objectives, evaluation, and pedagogy
misconceptions.feedback: AI can amplify good design, but it cannot rescue weak objectives, poor content structure, or missing evaluation by itself.

misconceptions.description: Reading Bloom's 2 Sigma Problem as proof that humans should be removed
misconceptions.trigger: learner concludes that one-to-one gains mean teachers are no longer needed
misconceptions.feedback: Bloom's result highlights the value of personalized support. It does not imply that human teaching, mentoring, and judgment are obsolete.

misconceptions.description: Assuming adaptive AI feedback does not need validation or logging
misconceptions.trigger: learner argues that personalized systems can be trusted without evidence or traceability
misconceptions.feedback: Adaptive systems need logging, evaluation, and quality checks precisely because they personalize instruction and can fail in subtle ways.
